reviews.review: one of the best games ever - really wish they had followed up with the sequel +
Good game, follows the Warhammer 40k lore very well.

Space Marine is one of the games I feel as though I get thoroughly dissolved into the game.  I am pretty sure there was a time when my wife heard me scream at the computer: "Booo ya, I AM A SPACE MARINE."  The controls are tight and the game just flows with you as you play along.  But a brief discussion on the game, in this 3rd person shooter you play as a Space Marine that has just arrived on the scene of an ork attack on a planet.  Your mission is to push back the tide and win the day, securing the planet for the Empire.

In short, this game has a lot going for it.  The visceral feel of combat has the biggest impact on the game in my opinion.  It helps set the tone for core gameplay that has you dispatching Orks in a ton of different ways, all of which are deeply gratifying to the player.  This feed back and gratification leads to the player feeling like they are a Space Marine!  To make a comparison, it feels like a Warhammer 40k version of Gears of War.  The gameplay isn't that dissimilar. 

The core of the gameplay is really the heart of the game and I can't find much to criticize on the gameplay itself.  This is why I would recommend it to anyone that has any interest in shooters and/or scifi games.  To me it is a 4/5 and I would recommend picking it up on a steam sale however as it is a bit dated graphically.

This game was phenomenal. I played it straight through and I haven't done that with a game in years. Great combat, great sound and a great story. The game makes you feel very powerful but also very weak when pitted against larger foes. You owe it to yourself to give this game a playthrough. Pick it up at regular price and you still won't be disappointed! I played @ 1440p and the tectues and quality was still amazing for a game made in 2011. On to the sequel!

A solid third person shooter. I appreciate that there is a health bar and no sticky cover. However, health pick ups would have been more useful rather than kills for health. These often prolonged kill animations that grant you health leave you exposed and you can lose just as much health as you gain in the process. Another issue is that the various pieces of cover you can use don't do a good job of protecting you, mainly from grenades. Grenades have awful trajectories and more than once I lost a portion of my shields to my own grenades because it hit a corner of rubble. Environments were a bit lackluster, I experienced a couple of glitches, one where I was stuck in a wall and had to reload a checkpoint, and in the other I phased through the map floor and fell to my death. Those were the only two I encountered besides the sound cutting off for split seconds a couple times--by no means game breaking. Other than, the checkpoints get a little cute. Sometimes you'll respawn right before the area you died in, and other times you're transported back to further back area and have to slog your way through a tedious mess of enemies. 

The story is pretty solid, although the characters are a bit paint-by-numbers. The action was nice and fun, the variety of weapons was good. Environments were a bit lackluster and narrow. The variety of enemies was awesome and I had to shift tactics a few time. A lot of door opening and elevator action, which was more amusing to me than annoying. I make it seem like there's more good than bad, but honestly the good has more weight than the bad. It was fun, it was engaging for the most part, and by the end I felt attached to our lead character. Nothing incredible but by no means a bad game; try it out of you want to kil some time with a challenging shooter.
